messages:
nina: Quick design thread: proposal to make the 'Sample project' checklist step optionally auto-complete after a short demo-run. Flow: user clicks "Run demo" -> ephemeral sandbox opens -> when they click "Finish demo" we mark the step complete. This reduces friction for first-run users who just want to see output. Thoughts?

raj: I like lowering friction, but we need a clear signal they actually looked at the demo. Suggest requiring one interaction (e.g., click 'Next' in demo or run a single query) before auto-complete. Otherwise it's too easy to game.

claire: Research notes: people responded well to lightweight demos that felt like "taste tests". They preferred an explicit finish action over implicit timeouts. Also they liked a tiny success animation when a step completed. But we should avoid heavy gamification.

marc: Accessibility nits: whichever UI completes the step must announce the result with an aria-live region: e.g., "Step complete: Sample project demo finished." Also ensure the demo modal traps focus and returns focus to the checklist item.

nina: Good. UX question: do we show a small completion badge (check + microcopy "Demo run") on the checklist card, or animate the whole card into a compact 'completed' state?

raj: Compact completed state is cleaner and reduces write-ups on long lists. For discoverability, the badge should be visible on the collapsed checklist row.

claire: On copy: short microcopy for the CTA: current 'Try a sample project' -> consider 'Run demo' (short) and confirmation 'Demo finished' as the completion label. For accessibility include a longer alt: 'Run demo of sample project to see a quick end-to-end request and response.'

marc: Color/contrast: the green check used in mocks fails 3:1 when paired with light text in dark mode. Use an icon-only check with additional text color that passes AA, or use a stronger background (#0F7A5C) with white icon.

nina: Telemetry: events we want: `onboarding.sample.run_started`, `onboarding.sample.interaction`, `onboarding.sample.run_finished` and whether completion was user-initiated. Raj, can you add instrumentation notes?

raj: Yep. Will emit `onboarding.sample.run_finished` with properties {"completed": true/false, "interaction_count": n, "ephemeral_session_id": "..."}. We'll cap events for privacy and avoid sending any code/inputs.

claire: Minor UX add: show a one-line summary on the finished state like "Demo finished: tried inference with the 'Q&A' sample" so users know what they completed. That helps when they return later.

marc: Also ensure screen reader users hear that summary via aria-live. In addition, keyboard users should be able to undo the completion via a small 'Undo' button in the badge that reopens the demo.

nina: Poll time: do we prefer (A) explicit 'Finish demo' required to mark completed, (B) implicit auto-complete after interaction, or (C) no auto-complete (manual mark only)? React :one: for A, :two: for B, :three: for C

ux-bot: poll created: https://poll.company/ux/67890 (expires in 72h)

raj: :one:  (A) prefer explicit finish.

claire: :one:  (A) explicit.

marc: :one:  but with keyboard undo.

nina: Nice consensus. Action items: 1) Raj - add telemetry spec + event property whitelist 2) Marc - implement aria-live and focus flow, verify color tokens for completed badge 3) Claire - write final microcopy for CTA/confirmation and example summary 4) Nina - update onboarding epic with flow and link to poll. I'll attach updated comps shortly. Thanks! :sparkles:
